title: Period-equality conjecture for nim-sequences and zero-position sequences
statement:
Let $G$ be a subtraction game, let $\mathcal{G}(n)$ denote the nim-value of a pile of size $n$, and define the zero-position indicator sequence $\mathcal{V}(n)$ by

$$
\mathcal{V}(n)=
\begin{cases}
0,&\text{if }\mathcal{G}(n)=0;\\
1,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
$$

**Period-equality conjecture.** For every subtraction game, the sequences $\{\mathcal{G}(n)\}$ and $\{\mathcal{V}(n)\}$ have the same period $p$. Since subtraction-game nim-sequences are periodic, the indicator sequence is periodic as well; the conjecture asserts that passing to zero versus nonzero nim-values does not reduce the period. Its general status is open.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1202.2986

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2012).
source_name: Nhan Bao Ho, “On the expansion of three-element subtraction sets”, arXiv:1202.2986 (2014).
